decision: Services write events to an outbox table in the same transaction as their data; a CDC relay publishes them to Kafka
why: Dual writes (database then broker) lose events when the second write fails; the outbox makes 'saved' and 'published' the same fact.
alternative: Publish to Kafka from application code after commit.
value: No lost or phantom events, and replays are always possible.

decision: Events are partitioned by business key (order, return, account), shown as partition · offset on every row
why: Ordering only matters per key; keying keeps one order's events in sequence while the topic scales across partitions.
value: Consumers never see 'delivered' before 'label-created' for the same order.

decision: Actions people take (a refund at the counter) appear in the same tail, marked 'recorded by a person', and Counter links here by key
why: Support and ops ask 'did my refund go out?'; searching by the return id answers it without a ticket.
alternative: A separate audit screen per system.
value: One place to prove what happened, from any system.

decision: Clicking a key opens a drawer with the raw payload, schema version, idempotency key and every consumer it reached
why: Integration debugging is about the exact bytes and who received them; a drawer keeps the tail running behind it.
alternative: Navigate to an event detail page.
value: Debug without losing your place in a live stream.

decision: The tail samples high-volume topics (auth.scored) and runs on the in-browser world
why: A readable tail and $0 hosting beat a full firehose nobody can read.
alternative: Stream every event from a hosted broker to the browser.
value: Legible, live and free; pausable for anyone reading.
